steps.comment: The duel from the visitor's side: a bare attack is made with the sword in hand and says so; the figure's defenceless state draws the eye to the hood; the possessive is not read, and the hood is had by the figure's name instead; restart is refused in character.

expect.words: As in a dream, you see yourself tumbling down a great, dark staircase. All about you are shadowy images of struggles against fierce opponents and diabolical traps. These give way to another round of images: of imposing stone figures, a cool, clear lake, and, now, of an old, yet oddly youthful man. He turns toward you slowly, his long, silver hair dancing about him in a fresh breeze. "You have reached the final test, my friend! You are proved clever and powerful, but this is not yet enough! Seek me when you feel yourself worthy!" The dream dissolves around you as his last words echo through the void....
Endless Stair

You are at the bottom of a seemingly endless stair, winding its way upward beyond your vision. An eerie light, coming from all around you, casts strange shadows on the walls. To the south is a dark and winding trail.
Your old friend, the brass lantern, is at your feet.
Taken.
The lamp is now on.
Junction

You are at the junction of a north-south passage and an east-west passage. To the north, you can make out the bottom of a stairway. The ways to the east and south are relatively cramped, but a wider trail leads to the west.
Standing before you is a great rock. Imbedded within it is an Elvish sword.
Creepy Crawl
You are in a dark and quite creepy crawlway with passages leaving to the north, east, south, and southwest.
Land of Shadow
You are at the eastern end of a dark, featureless landscape of shallow hills. Paths to the east and southeast reenter the rock.
Time passes...
Through the shadows, a cloaked and hooded figure appears before you, blocking the northern exit from the room and carrying a brightly glowing sword.
From nowhere, the sword from the junction appears in your hand, wildly glowing!
(with the sword)
A good parry! Your sword wounds the hooded figure!
The figure has a light wound which hasn't affected its seemingly great strength.
The hooded figure stabs nonchalantly with its sword and misses.
(with the sword)
A good parry! Your sword wounds the hooded figure!
The figure has some wounds and is probably not capable of hindering your movement.
The hooded figure stabs nonchalantly with its sword and misses.
(with the sword)
A good parry! Your sword wounds the hooded figure!
The figure is hurt, and its strength appears to be fading.
The hooded figure attempts a thrust, but its weakened state prevents hitting you.
(with the sword)
A quick stroke catches the hooded figure off guard! Blood trickles down the figure's arm!
The figure appears to be badly hurt and defenseless.
It lowers its sword, and its head with it, and waits.
The hooded figure attempts a thrust, but its weakened state prevents hitting you.

A figure in a hood and a cloak, both dark, both plain, standing the way you stand and holding its sword the way you hold yours, which you had not noticed you did until now. The hood casts a shadow where a face should be, and the sword glows with the same cold blue light as your own. It is watching you; you can feel it watching you, as you can feel yourself watching it.
The hooded figure appears to be badly hurt and defenseless.

It has stopped fighting the way you fight; it has stopped fighting at all. It stands with the point of its sword in the ground and its head bowed, and the hood, which has kept its face from you all this while, hangs within reach of your hand.
The hooded figure attempts a thrust, but its weakened state prevents hitting you.

The shadows lie across the hills in the wrong places, long where nothing stands to throw them, and some of them, when you look away, seem to have moved. It is a land named for them, and it has earned the name.
The hooded figure attempts a thrust, but its weakened state prevents hitting you.
Two paths leave the hills to the east and southeast and go back into the rock, where there is a roof over your head again. From here they look like the mouths of burrows.
The hooded figure attempts a thrust, but its weakened state prevents hitting you.
The passage is cut through the rock, and goes where it goes. The ways out of here are described above, and you may take any of them.
The hooded figure attempts a thrust, but its weakened state prevents hitting you.
You can't see any such thing.

You slowly remove the hood from your badly wounded opponent and recoil in horror at the sight of your own face, weary and wounded. A faint smile comes to the lips and then the face starts to change, very slowly, into that of an old, wizened person. The image fades and with it the body of your hooded opponent. The cloak remains on the ground.
Your sword is no longer glowing.

This world does not start over on request. What you have lost stays lost, and what you have done stays done. The stair is to the north of wherever you are, more or less; and the old man will carry you back to it, with your lamp, such as it is, three times, and the fourth time he will keep you, which is as near to an ending as a lost visitor gets.
You are carrying:
A lamp (providing light)
An Elvish sword
A hood (being worn)
